lines.x: The International Monetary Fund warned that Kazakhstan's large-scale construction program could fuel consumer inflation unless extensive public spending is matched by commensurate productivity gains.
Official figures show Kazakhstan exported 5.06 million tonnes of crude oil and bituminous products to France in Jan-Sept 2026, up 33.98% year-on-year.
According to Eni's World Energy Review, Kazakhstan increased oil and coal production during 2025, while natural gas and copper output recorded declines.
Kazakhstan's crude oil and condensate extraction dropped 6.8% year-on-year in the first ten months of 2026, while domestic natural gas output declined by 9%, official data showed.
